# Code Review — PR #170: Pipeline Primitives

**Branch:** `feat/issue-160-pipeline-primitives`
**Reviewer:** Claude Sonnet 4.6
**Date:** 2026-04-24

---

## Review Summary

PR #170 adds `src/presentation/pipeline_primitives.py` — three asyncio-backed presentation-layer primitives (`ApprovalGate`, `TokenStreamBus`, `WikiContextBus`) that decouple the future Python-native orchestrator from any specific transport or UI. The implementation is clean, well-tested (6 passing unit tests, all passing), and consistent with the project's import conventions. Documentation is thorough and accurate. Two warnings were found: a dead `_closed` flag that signals an incomplete post-close guard, and an undocumented single-consumer constraint on both buses that silently breaks under multi-consumer use.

**Files Reviewed:** 5
**Findings:** 0 Critical, 2 Warning, 2 Suggestion

---

## Findings

### Warning Findings

```
[W-01] _closed flag is dead code — emit() after close() silently loses items
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/presentation/pipeline_primitives.py
Lines: 65-85 (TokenStreamBus), 103-125 (WikiContextBus)
Description: Both buses set self._closed = True inside close(), but emit() and
_iterate() never read this flag. Items enqueued after close() are placed after
the sentinel in the queue; iteration stops at the sentinel and post-close items
are silently unreachable. The presence of the flag implies a guard was intended
but not implemented.
Suggestion: Add a guard to emit() in both classes:
    async def emit(self, delta: str) -> None:
        if self._closed:
            raise RuntimeError("emit() called after close()")
        await self._queue.put(delta)
Or, if post-close emit is designed to be a no-op, document that intent and
remove the unreachable queue puts via an early return. The current state
(flag set, never read) is an incomplete implementation.
```

```
[W-02] Single-consumer assumption undocumented on both buses
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/presentation/pipeline_primitives.py
Lines: 72-85 (TokenStreamBus._iterate), 112-125 (WikiContextBus._iterate)
Description: __aiter__ creates a new generator per call, but both generators
share a single asyncio.Queue. With two concurrent consumers, queue items are
distributed arbitrarily between them, and only one consumer receives the
_SENTINEL, leaving the other blocked indefinitely on queue.get(). Nothing in
the code or docstrings declares single-consumer as a constraint.

asyncio.Queue does not support fan-out. If the planned TUI and an internal
logging consumer both iterate the same TokenStreamBus concurrently, one will
hang. No current call sites in this PR exhibit this pattern, but the absence
of the constraint note means a future author has no indication the usage is
unsafe.
Suggestion: Add a brief note to both bus docstrings, e.g.:
    "Supports a single consumer only. Concurrent iteration over the same bus
     is not supported and will cause one consumer to block indefinitely."
Or if fan-out is eventually required, replace asyncio.Queue with an
asyncio-native multicast pattern (e.g., a list of per-consumer queues
populated in emit()).
```

---

### Suggestions

```
[S-01] resolve() called before await_decision() silently discards the decision
Category: Correctness
Severity: Suggestion
File: src/presentation/pipeline_primitives.py
Lines: 28-32
Description: resolve() guards on `self._future is not None`. If the TUI resolves
the gate before the orchestrator has called await_decision() (e.g., due to an
ordering race or misconfigured startup), self._future is None, the guard passes
silently, the decision is discarded, and the gate blocks forever when
await_decision() is later called.

In the intended usage flow this race cannot occur, but there is no test
confirming the resolve-before-await path, and no docstring note making the
constraint explicit.
Suggestion: Either document the precondition ("resolve() must only be called
after await_decision() has been awaited") or add a deferred-set design: store
the decision in an instance var if no future is pending and return it
immediately from the next await_decision() call.
```

```
[S-02] No test coverage for post-close emit or resolve-before-await
Category: Testing
Severity: Suggestion
File: tests/unit/test_pipeline_primitives.py
Lines: general
Description: W-01 and S-01 above identify two edge cases that are not covered
by the test suite: (1) calling emit() after close() and observing that items
are lost (or an error is raised, per the intended guard), and (2) calling
resolve() before await_decision() and observing that the gate does not silently
drop the decision. Exercising these cases would both validate the intended
contract and expose the current incomplete implementation.
Suggestion: Add:
    test_emit_after_close_raises_or_drops — call bus.close(), then bus.emit(...),
    then consume; verify no post-close items arrive (or an error is raised).

    test_resolve_before_await_decision_does_not_deadlock — call gate.resolve(...)
    first, then gate.await_decision(); verify it returns rather than blocking.
```

---

## Overall Assessment

The implementation is sound and ready to serve as a foundation for the Python-native orchestrator. The primitives are well-designed, correctly typed (mypy: no issues), and all six unit tests pass. The review found no regressions or correctness bugs within the documented usage patterns. Two warnings highlight incomplete invariant enforcement (`_closed` flag is set but never enforced, single-consumer constraint is implicit) that should be resolved before other contributors build consumers on top of these buses. Neither warning blocks merging if the project is the sole immediate consumer and the patterns are addressed before the pipeline orchestrator is wired in. The two suggestions cover defensive testing for edge cases that fall outside current tests. Documentation quality is high and accurately reflects the implementation.
